chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a man who intentionally killed a man, while the one killed had his right hand severed. So he said:

If his hand had been cut off due to an offense that he committed against himself, or he had been cut and had taken the compensation for his hand from the one who cut it off, then if his heirs wish to kill his killer, they must pay to the heirs of his killer the blood-money of the hand by which equality was deficient, and then kill him. And if they wish, they may deduct the blood-money of his hand from him and take the remainder.

He said: If his hand had been cut off without an offense that he committed against himself, and no compensation had been taken for it, they may kill his killer and he is not liable for anything. And if they wish, they may take the full blood-money. Thus did we find it in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: his legal heirs or avengers entitled to pursue the claim
key_terms.جِنَايَةٍ: an offense or injurious act carrying legal consequence
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial compensation for unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the written legal record attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of qiṣāṣ if the murder victim had a severed right hand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on qiṣāṣ when the murdered person had previously lost his right hand. If that loss was due to his own offense or had already been compensated through diyah, the heirs must account for the missing hand in retaliation or settlement; otherwise, they may execute the killer without additional payment or take full diyah. The report attributes this ruling to the legal record known as the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.
